mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior month reduces discount rates applied to expected corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2%, the S&P 500 anticipates a future Fed rate hike cycle, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative 60-day forward returns.
regime_hint: accelerating inflation in the core economy
failure_condition: In a regime with CPIAUCSL > 2% for > 3 months, the 60-day SPX forward return is positive with p < 0.05 in a t-test.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 3% signals tight labor markets that drive wage-price spirals, prompting firms to raise prices and eroding S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% in a month
failure_condition: Payrolls growth remains below 3% for 4 consecutive months with no significant negative SPX 5-day forward returns (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 personal consumption turns above the 5-year moving average, it indicates a shift toward stronger demand that supports corporate earnings growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 5-year moving average not clearly defined due to insufficient history; or GDPC1 above SMA but SPX 20-day returns flat (no statistical significance).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO supply expansion exceeding 2% suggests easing supply constraints that reduce production costs and boost earnings expectations, yielding positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth ≤ 2% for 6 consecutive months with no significant positive 60-day SPX returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in UNRATE above 0.2% indicate weakening labor market strength, which reduces wage growth expectations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises in 2 consecutive months each by more than 0.1%
failure_condition: UNRATE remains below 0.2% for 3 months with no negative SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly RSAFS retail sales growth exceeds 4%, it reflects robust consumer demand that firms interpret as a signal to raise guidance and equity valuations, resulting in positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by more than 1% in a month
failure_condition: RSAFS > 4% but SPX 5-day returns are flat or negative (no Granger causality).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising), the interaction between FEDFUNDS and HOUST (housing starts) where HOUST lags FEDFUNDS by 1 month, produces negative 20-day SPX returns as higher rates suppress credit expansion and housing momentum.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases while HOUST lags by 1 month
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with lagged housing starts
failure_condition: In a tightening regime, HOUST does not lag FEDFUNDS and SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
